0.long_answer: Cytomegalovirus (CMV), a member of the herpesvirus family, has an icosahedral capsid that displays T=16 symmetry. It is the leading non-genetic cause of congenital deafness and ambulatory problems because it can be transmitted vertically from a pregnant woman to her fetus. In congenital CMV (cCMV) infection, the virus crosses the placenta and infects the developing fetus, which may result in sensorineural hearing loss and motor deficits among other potential neurological complications. Early diagnosis and intervention are crucial in managing the long-term effects associated with this viral infection.
